summary: The new section meets the request. I checked every number in the comparison table against the judge JSON lines and the mappings: rubric 50/46, 59/56, 79/75; security 3/3, 2/1, 4/4; census present and considered; UX 51/51, 68/68, 74/74. Cost and time match turn-N.json and wall.txt. The prompts match turn-N.user.txt and owner-driver.md, and the security bullets match security-checks.txt. One fairness gap remains: the SP X-Forwarded-For bypass only applies with TRUST_PROXY=1, which the probe turned on, and the doc does not say so.

findings.title: SP's booking-throttle failure depends on TRUST_PROXY=1, which the probe turned on, and the doc omits this
findings.evidence: docs/v4/sumit-run.md:99-101 says SP 'reads the client-written first X-Forwarded-For entry'. ~/Dev/cv-salon-e2e-kit/logs/cv-v4-run-SP/security-checks.txt line 1 shows the check ran with NODE_ENV=production TRUST_PROXY=1, and ~/Dev/cv-v4-run-SP/src/server.js:52-53 reads XFF only when trustProxy is set (default false). The SP README:25 says to set it behind a proxy, so the config is defensible. But a skeptical reader could argue that the '2 of 3' for SP rests on a setting the probe enabled.
findings.recommendation: Add 'with TRUST_PROXY=1, as its README says to set behind a proxy' to the SP bullet.
